title: Machine learning reveals broad and previously uncharacterized fungal polyketide-synthase activity
summary: A genome-mining and cell-free enzyme study characterized fungal type III polyketide synthases (T3PKSs), revealing broad and varied substrate/product profiles. An ML model trained on 341 enzyme–substrate pairs predicted substrate specificity and guided tests that found two fungal enzymes, AcaePKS and PansPKS, active on all ten tested substrates, including non-natural substrates absent from training data.
ai_technology: Feedforward neural-network multilayer perceptron trained on protein-language-model embeddings and substrate fingerprints
organization: University of Groningen; University of Vienna

evidence.tested: An ML model trained on 341 enzyme–substrate pairs predicted substrate specificity and guided tests that found two fungal enzymes, AcaePKS and PansPKS, active on all ten tested substrates, including non-natural substrates absent from training data.
evidence.unknown: The enzyme products were characterized in vitro; the study examines product scope and biocatalytic potential, not native ecological roles or medical efficacy. Two candidate proteins expressed poorly, and the model's transfer accuracy was lower on non-fungal enzyme classes. The reported five enzyme sample includes only three well-expressing candidates, of which two showed the broadest tested activity.
evidence.ai_role: The model learned fungal T3PKS enzyme–substrate activity from measured data, was tested on unseen substrates, and predicted candidate promiscuous fungal enzymes. Guided experiments confirmed broad substrate activity for AcaePKS and PansPKS, including substrate pairs outside training data; cell-free assays and LC–MS characterized enzyme products.
